decision: Defined completion as current direct dependencies plus a successful image build and full validation
why: The image combines about 30 pins with version-coupled patches, so registry freshness alone cannot prove compatibility

decision: Treat resolver-selected transitive packages as owned by the refreshed base and direct dependency solves
why: Blanket upgrades after the solve would break the base image contract and make the build non-reproducible
result: direct pins and fresh solves in scope

decision: Use a small catalog-backed direct-declaration auditor with semantic locators and exception-only holds
why: The design arena preferred explicit authority ownership but rejected duplicated versions, line locators, and a general parser framework

decision: Moved the runtime to base 2026-09-07 and advanced every compatible direct pin found by the live audit
why: The audit now reports all supported declarations current or explicitly held and the base tag is multi-architecture

decision: Kept Notebook Intelligence 5.3.1, MCP below 2, Jupyter Collaboration 4.4.2, ipykernel 6.31.0, and pnpm 11
why: NBI 5.4 conflicts with the ACP protocol range; Jupyter AI 3.2 requires Collaboration below 5; the remaining holds protect documented build and comm contracts

decision: Refresh apt runtime packages with dist-upgrade and direct pip distributions with --upgrade
why: This updates packages inherited from the fresh base without an unbounded pip-over-conda rewrite of the tested Jupyter environment
result: fresh OS and direct Python solve enabled

decision: Use the Apache binary-distribution index as the Tomcat release authority
why: The Git tag for 11.0.26 existed before Apache published a matching binary archive, so a source tag was not an installable image release
result: Tomcat held at the latest published binary 11.0.25

decision: Anchor jupyterlab-slurm to a reviewed commit and migrate its obsolete builder dependency during the image build
why: The upstream main commit still names @jupyterlab/builder while current JupyterLab requires @jupyter/builder; an exact source assertion makes upstream drift fail closed
result: local wheel prototype and focused tests pass

decision: Patch Lightcone CLI 0.4.2 source to accept ASTRA Tools 0.2.17 and its idempotent init callback
why: The latest stable Lightcone release pins ASTRA Tools 0.2.11 exactly, while Lightcone 0.5 remains a release candidate with a changed execution model
result: isolated tool install, pip check, version check, and lc init prototype pass

decision: Retain agent-skills commit 4ded682 and rewrite its historical ASTRA pins at build time
why: Current upstream removed the stable reproduction plugin in favor of a workflow requiring unreleased Lightcone 0.5; the retained workflow is compatible with existing Slurm templates
result: plugin installs for Codex and Claude and complete skill closure for OpenCode pass in image build

decision: Built the complete image from the 2026-09-07 base and refreshed package repositories
why: A clean base transition must exercise OS, Python, npm, frontend, agent, and workflow layers together

decision: Pin Snakemake 9.26.1 and Packaging 25.0 in both the main and isolated Lightcone environments
why: Packaging 26.3 made both resolvers silently backtrack from the current user-facing workflow CLI; the infrastructure library can safely yield to Snakemake's declared packaging<26 bound
result: both environments resolve Snakemake 9.26.1 and pass dependency checks

decision: Make installed image tests and examples world-readable
why: The restrictive checkout umask produced root-owned mode-0600 test files, so the intended jovyan image test could not collect them even though the image built
result: jovyan collected and ran the complete installed suite

decision: Keep immutable Claude and Codex fallbacks while selecting user-managed binaries from the persistent home
why: Users need unprivileged updates that survive image replacement without sacrificing a known-good binary for fresh or read-only homes
result: actual claude update and codex update created home binaries and selectors executed them

decision: Pin Claude Code 2.1.267 instead of relying on the native installer's stable alias
why: The final live updater probe found stable had installed 2.1.236 while the official release stream and claude update reported 2.1.267
result: live audit and final image both report Claude Code 2.1.267

decision: Validate the exact final image and source tree
why: Completion requires runtime behavior, dependency consistency, and extension compatibility rather than a successful build alone
result: 591 unit tests and 155 container tests passed; 16 environment skips; apt and both Python environments current/consistent; Jupyter extensions OK

decision: Clarify that Python validation proves dependency consistency, not registry freshness for every transitive distribution
why: The final inventory has 40 distributions below their registry latest; these are resolver-selected/base packages and documented compatibility families rather than stale audited direct pins
result: apt has no pending updates; every tracked direct dependency is current or explicitly held; both Python environments pass dependency checks

decision: Record current embedded pins that the declaration auditor does not yet discover
why: nf-test and the Julia static strace artifact use installer/URL forms outside the supported ARG and Python-requirement grammar
result: independent release-authority review confirms nf-test 0.9.5 and strace 6.7.0+1 remain current
